The trigger that should be recording customer changes is **`customers_audit`** on `public.customers`. It is **DISABLED**. Its definition is `AFTER UPDATE ON public.customers FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION log_customer_change()`. Because the disabled state stops it from firing, updates to customers aren't being written to the audit log. The trigger only covers UPDATE, so INSERT and DELETE on customers were never audited by this trigger. I haven't changed anything. If you want it back on, someone with the right privileges would run `ALTER TABLE public.customers ENABLE TRIGGER customers_audit;`. Before doing that, it's worth finding out who disabled it and why, in case it was intentional (for example, during a bulk load or migration).
